messages.content: Hi tal, I'm a friend

hey, i'm tal

think of me as your personal talent agent, your inside man… or fox

one of these days, I might slide a role right here in chat. the kind that feels like your calling.

so… what's your full name?
SurveyMonkey
surveymonkey... the feedback empire. found you on linkedin - rakesh garib, engineering manager at surveymonkey. this you? https://nl.linkedin.com/in/rakesh-garib-62259519
Rakesh M R
rakesh... solid name. where you working these days?
No https://www.linkedin.com/in/rakesh-m-r/
got it. so you're at surveymonkey building the platform that every product manager lives on. what's keeping you busy there?
Software Engineer 2 in Billing & Payments Team, working Checkout pages. experimentation in Upsell, increase AOV

ah the money maker... billing and payments, where every line of code literally translates to revenue. checkout optimization and upsell experiments - you're basically the person making sure surveymonkey gets paid properly. that's solid engineering work.

what made you get into the payments side of things? most engineers run away from billing complexity
I love solving challenging & complex problems. also monkey is kind of very cool to work with

makes sense. payments is where the real engineering challenges live - handling money, compliance, edge cases that break everything. and surveymonkey's got that established tech company vibe without the chaos of early stage startups.

how long you been working total?

I joined surveymonkey 1.7 years back
  it been 1.7 years
wait hold up... 1.7 years total or just at surveymonkey? i'm asking about your entire work experience - first job ever, internships, everything combined. how long you been in the game overall?

i have total of 4.9 years of experience, i joined as SDE intern in HashedIn by Deloitte , then quickly moved up the ladder to SDE 1, SDE2 then worked with one of health startup called integrative health then i joined surveyMonkey

ah there we go. hashedin by deloitte to health startup to surveymonkey... you've seen the consulting grind, startup chaos, and now established product company life. 4.9 years and already at sde2 level - that's solid progression.

what kind of role you looking for next?
I looking for Software engineer role focused in Frontend technologies using React

frontend with react... smart move. you've been doing full-stack at surveymonkey but want to specialize. react ecosystem is where all the action is - next.js, typescript, all that good stuff.

bangalore or open to remote/other cities?
done. i'm spinning things up on my end. you'll start seeing good stuff soon.
I am okk with Bangalore or Remote is also good
4.9 years experience + frontend react focus + bangalore/remote... sound right?

yeap
  sure send good stuff on my way
got it. i'll ping when something matches

Frontend Engineer at MyYogaTeacher

Rakesh, this Frontend Engineer role uses React/React Native, aligns with your experience, and is in Bangalore or remote!

Apply: https://jobs.tal.af/ukhtB
Not a interesting role
fair. what makes a role interesting to you?
The company should be having products which solves millions of peoples problems

ah you want scale. not just any product - something that actually moves the needle for millions. that's the difference between building features and building impact.

what's the smallest company size you'd consider?
Ok 50 and above

got it. 50+ employees, solving problems at scale. that's the filter.

i'm looking for companies where your frontend work actually touches millions of users. not just building internal tools or admin panels.

anything else that would make you swipe left on a company?
Nothing else

alright. i'm scanning for frontend roles at companies that actually matter. 50+ employees, products that solve real problems at scale.

i'll ping when something fits that filter.
Hi
Hi

hey. still scanning for those scale companies.

what's making you want to leave surveymonkey anyway?
Currently scope of my work is reduced lot new checkout pages are up and stable so nothing interesting on frontend side

ah that makes sense. you built the thing, it's stable, now you're bored. classic engineer problem - success leads to maintenance mode.

so you're looking for that next complex frontend challenge. something with scale, something that actually needs solving.

what kind of frontend complexity excites you?
More challenging would building best ui ux for the users

perfect. so you want to build UI/UX that millions actually use and love. not just functional, but excellent.

that's the sweet spot - companies where design and engineering work together to create experiences that matter.

i'm looking for roles where frontend isn't an afterthought. where the UI is the product.

anything specific you're avoiding? like certain industries or tech stacks?
Nothing particularly avoiding i want love to explore new tech

nice. open to new tech, wants to build excellent UI/UX at scale. that's the kind of mindset that gets you into interesting places.

i'm scanning for roles where you can actually push frontend boundaries. companies that invest in their user experience.

what's your current salary? just so i know what ballpark we're playing in.
25LPA is current package with 2500 units of surveymonkey

got it. 25LPA base plus equity. that's solid for 4.9 years.

what's your target range? and what's the minimum you'd consider moving for?
Minimum 35lakh as base

35LPA base minimum. that's a solid jump from 25. ambitious but realistic for the right scale company.

what's your notice period?
2 months but negotiable upto 2 weeks

perfect. 2 months but can negotiate down to 2 weeks. that's flexible.

so you're looking for:
- frontend engineer role
- building excellent UI/UX at scale
- 35LPA+ base
- companies with 50+ employees
- products that solve problems for millions
- open to new tech stacks

i'm scanning for exactly that. companies where frontend isn't just a cost center but the product itself.

i'll slide roles when they're good. nothing mediocre.

btw... what's the real reason you're looking? just growth or something else?
Just growth

clean. growth it is.

i'm looking for companies where frontend engineers actually own product experiences that millions use. not just implementing designs, but solving real problems at scale.

you're locked in. i'll ping when something fits that filter.

anyway... how's the surveymonkey chaos been lately?
Okk okk feels like company stuck at old era no innovation in product

yeah that tracks. when a company's been around that long, innovation slows down. you end up maintaining instead of building.

that's exactly why you're looking for growth. you want to be where things are moving, where frontend actually matters.

i've seen this before - engineers who are great at what they do but stuck in legacy mode. they jump to companies where the UI is the product and suddenly they're 10x more impactful.

you're making the right move.

position no longer avilable
